ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards: All directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the New Zealand sanctions registers administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit advisory lists. Section 14 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 requires risk-rating and enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons of domestic and foreign origin, including beneficial ownership tracing through a look-through ultimate shareholder register maintained under s 90 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Registers of Ultimate Shareholders) Regulations 2022. The screening protocol must be documented in the AML/CFT compliance programme before incorporation is completed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Registration and Name Reservation Portal (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies/register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be expressed in Latin script and must contain the word 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation such as 'Ltd' as the final word. Names in non-Latin scripts are not registrable and must be transliterated into English/Latin characters. Te reo Maori orthography, including long-vowel macrons, is accepted by the Companies Register. Punctuation is limited to a specified set of characters including ampersands, parentheses, plus signs, hyphens, slashes, and full stops, and the name must not consist solely of generic or geographic descriptors without a distinctive element.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office declines a proposed name under ss 19-21 of the Companies Act 1993 on grounds of identical or almost identical similarity, misleading character, or failure to obtain the requisite ministerial or regulatory consent, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request through the Companies Office customer service channel within 10 working days of the rejection. Where the rejection is founded on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant may seek ministerial or portfolio-authority consent (e.g., the Minister of Finance or the Reserve Bank of New Zealand for 'Bank' or 'Finance' tokens, and the Financial Markets Authority for 'Insurance' and 'Trust' tokens). If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the decision is reviewable as a prescribed decision by way of judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. An accelerated alternative is to file a revised name with a distinctive distinguishing element and pay an additional name reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for satisfying the registered office obligation under s 213 of the Companies Act 1993, provided the virtual office provider supplies a physical street address in New Zealand (not a PO Box) that is capable of receiving legal process and official correspondence. However, for an ISIC 6619 electronic money institution requiring a statutory financial services licence, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and the Financial Markets Authority expect genuine local management, a locally resident AML/CFT compliance officer, and substantive operational premises as conditions of licensing; a purely virtual-office structure without any local staffing or business substance will be commercially and regulatorily inadequate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For an AML/CFT reporting entity engaged in electronic money issuance and virtual IBAN reserve management, the likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or the Department of Internal Affairs within the first 24 months of licensed operation is estimated at 65-80%. A shell entity lacking local staff, local records, or a physical operational presence materially increases this probability and the attendant risk of licence suspension.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: New Zealand Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), sections 10–14 (formation and incorporation), 16–19 (legal capacity and name restrictions), 122–123 (registered office), 129–161 (board governance and officer appointment), 185–201 (share capital and capital maintenance), 215–224 (financial reporting), 378–380 (annual return requirements); supplemented by the Income Tax Act 2007 for non-resident tax classification, the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013, and the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2006. The 'International Company' (IC) designation is recognized by the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Office international company practice, permitting non-resident incorporation with a New Zealand agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, an agency of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online filing exclusively via the Companies Office Connect portal (connect.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 — 'Application for Registration as a Company', accompanied by Form NZCN2 (Consent to Act as Shareholder), Form NZCN3 (Consent to Act as Director), Form NZCN4 (Consent to Act as Registered Office Agent), and the optional Company Constitution; all submitted electronically through the Companies Office Connect portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under the Companies Act 1993; the International Company may be incorporated with a nominal issued capital of one (1) share of no par value at NZD 1.00 per share subscribed by the non-resident beneficial owner. However, for the Electronic Money Institution (EMI) operating license, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and the Financial Markets Authority conditionally require a minimum regulatory capital of NZD 500,000 (approximately USD 300,000), which must be fully paid into a segregated escrow account maintained with a New Zealand registered bank under a tripartite escrow agreement, releaseable only upon the satisfaction of all statutory formation and licensing obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

COMPANY: [INSERT COMPANY FULL LEGAL NAME] (the "Company") — New Zealand International Company (IC)
STATUTORY BASIS: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 10, 14, 122, 129, 152, 161, 185 and 200.
DATE AND MODE: This resolution is adopted by the subscriber/sole incorporator as a written resolution, executed in counterparts and circulated to all directors named herein, and is effective as of the date of incorporation.

RESOLVED, that:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The subscriber shares as stated in Form NZCN1 (Application for Registration), namely [number] ordinary shares of no par value issued to [Subscriber Name] at an issue price of NZD [amount] per share, be and are hereby ratified, confirmed and entered into the share register; the unpaid portion of the subscription price, if any, shall be called at the sole discretion of the board.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company in New Zealand is fixed at [street address, city, New Zealand], and the Board appoints [registered agent/office] as the designated agent for service of process; the Board hereby directs the Company Secretary to file Form NZCN5 (Notification of Registered Office) with the Registrar of Companies within one (1) business day.

3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The following persons be and are hereby appointed to the offices set opposite their names, each to hold office under sections 152 and 161 of the Companies Act 1993 until the next annual meeting or until earlier resignation or removal: [Name] — Managing Director; [Name] — Finance Director / Chief Risk Officer; [Name] — Company Secretary; [Name] — AML/CFT Compliance Officer.

4. BANKING AND ESCROW: The Directors are authorized to open and operate bank accounts (including a segregated client money / electronic money custody account) with a New Zealand registered bank and to execute a tripartite escrow agreement for the purpose of satisfying the NZD 500,000 minimum regulatory capital requirement imposed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand in connection with the application for the Electronic Money / Stored Value Facility authorization.

5. LICENSING INITIATION: The Directors are authorized to file, sign and prosecute the Financial Service Provider registration, AML/CFT registration and Reserve Bank of New Zealand authorization applications described in this dossier.

6. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution shall be effective immediately and a copy shall be entered in the company records; the chairperson is authorized to certify it.

DECLARED AND ADOPTED on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies (online portal: connect.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search against the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry; complete the online 'Reserve a Company Name' application through the Connect portal; pay the reservation fee by approved credit card; the name reservation is valid for 20 working days and may be renewed once for a further 20 working days.
required_dossiers: Reserve Company Name application form
Consent letter from any existing holder of a similar registered name (if required)
Trademark search certificate or due diligence record against the Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ) register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar considers the name objectionable, misleading, or contravening section 18 of the Companies Act 1993, a provisional refusal notice is issued; the applicant may submit a written submission to the Registrar within 20 working days, or alternatively reserve a revised name; an adverse final decision is appealable to the High Court of New Zealand under section 32.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel / International Company secretary (internal or external law firm admitted in New Zealand)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Company Constitution in writing in accordance with sections 14 and 15 of the Companies Act 1993; prepare all consents (Forms NZCN2, NZCN3, NZCN4) in English; the non-resident subscriber's execution may be made by counterparts, with signature pages notarized by a Commonwealth notary or apostilled under the Hague Convention; the registered agent confirms the principal place of administration outside New Zealand to preserve the International Company designation.
required_dossiers: Draft Company Constitution (including share transfer pre-emption rights and EMI reserve governance)
Form NZCN2 (Consent to Act as Shareholder)
Form NZCN3 (Consent to Act as Director)
Form NZCN4 (Consent to Act as Registered Office Agent)
Notarized or apostilled passport copies of subscriber(s) and beneficial owner(s)
Address verification and source of funds declaration for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected for incomplete signatures or notarization, the legal counsel must resubmit corrected pages within 5 working days; missing notarization may be cured by a statutory declaration or deed poll executed by the subscriber and filed with the Registrar as an affidavit in lieu.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Electronic Registration Desk (Connect portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full incorporation package electronically on the Connect portal, attaching the constitution, all consents, the registered office address statement, and the director/shareholder particulars; pay the statutory registration fee of NZD 150 (approximately USD 90); upon pre-validation the Registrar issues an electronic acknowledgement and, once satisfied, registers the company and issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Form NZCN1 (Application for Registration as a Company)
Form NZCN2 (Consent to Act as Shareholder)
Form NZCN3 (Consent to Act as Director)
Form NZCN4 (Consent to Act as Registered Office Agent)
Company Constitution (PDF version with signature pages)
Proof of registered office address in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried (for example, constitution non-compliance with section 14 or defective consent forms), the Companies Office issues an electronic query; the applicant has 20 working days to remedy the defect via the portal; if unresolved, the application lapses and the fee is forfeited; resubmission is permitted as a new application with a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, and Register Extraction
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies (automatic data exchange with the New Zealand Business Number registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allocates the NZBN; the company secretary retrieves the certified computerized extract from the Companies Office corporate extract system; the registered office agent files Form NZCN5 within 1 business day of the incorporation date, and any appointment of a New Zealand auditor or secretary is filed within 10 working days; the International Company designation is recorded against the company's entry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by the Register)
NZBN confirmation certificate
Computerized extract of the Companies Register
Form NZCN5 (Notification of Registered Office)
Director and shareholder register entries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any error in the Certificate (name, date, entity type, or registered office) is rectified by written application to the Registrar under section 12(5) of the Companies Act 1993; the Registrar issues an amended certificate within 5 working days; if the NZBN is not generated automatically, the company applies for a manual NZBN via the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and IRD Number Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRDNZ), Business Registration team (online portal: myIR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, GST, and any applicable PAYE/FBT using the Business Registration profile in myIR, cross-referencing the NZBN and directors' IRD numbers; obtain the New Zealand IRD number; submit the International Company declaration to confirm non-resident tax status (only New Zealand-sourced income is taxable, subject to the Income Tax Act 2007); open a separate GST input file for any future New Zealand supplies.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation
Directors' and beneficial owners' passport copies and IRD numbers
Registered office address proof
EMI business plan and projected revenue streams
Shareholder register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD business registration application is denied or suspended, the company must engage the IRD Business Integrity Team and submit a rectification letter plus complete beneficial-ownership disclosures within 20 working days; persistent failures may be handled by the High Court, but interim the company may apply for a determination under section 91 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) — Financial Service Providers Register (register.fsp.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic FSP application under service classes covering electronic money services, digital wallet storage, virtual IBAN issuance, and payment processing; designate a New Zealand-based principal contact/agent; pay the FMA registration and annual levy; append the AML/CFT compliance program; the FMA will issue the FSP number and certificate after fit-and-proper review of all directors and the beneficial owner.
required_dossiers: FSP application form (online)
Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
AML/CFT compliance program (section 57 of the AML/CFT Act 2009)
Fit-and-proper declarations (six-point verification for each director and senior manager)
Business plan and target-payment-rail strategy
Organisation chart and outsourced service provider register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA issues a query or intention to decline on fit-and-proper grounds (sections 20–22 of the FSP Act 2008), the applicant may submit a written explanation and supporting evidence within 15 working days; an adverse decision is reviewable by the District Court; interim relief may be obtained by requesting an FMA reconsideration with strengthened governance and independent director appointments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) — AML/CFT Group, in coordination with the Financial Markets Authority as joint supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a reporting entity on the DIA AML/CFT supervision system; file the Business Risk Assessment and the AML/CFT Compliance Programme; appoint a New Zealand-resident AML/CFT Compliance Officer; operationalize the full customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), sanctions screening, and suspicious transaction reporting framework under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2011; schedule the independent annual audit of the AML/CFT programme.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT registration statement (online DIA form)
Business entity risk assessment
AML/CFT compliance programme
Certificate of Incorporation and FSP registration number
Identity documents of the AML/CFT Compliance Officer and Board
AML/CFT audit engagement letter (independent external auditor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The DIA may return the registration with a request for correction; the filer must correct the non-conformity within 20 working days; if the registration is refused, the company may apply to the DIA for an exemption (sections 157–157B of the AML/CFT Act) or commence judicial review; failure to register is a strict liability offence, but active remediation and voluntary disclosure mitigate regulatory action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Stored Value / Electronic Money Authorization and Escrow Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) — Prudential Supervision Department, Banking and Payment Systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full prudential licensing package for the issuance of virtual IBANs and digital wallet reserve management, characterized as a Non-bank Deposit Taker (Stored Value Facility) under the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013 and Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2006; deliver the board-approved governance charter, capital adequacy statement, escrow arrangement, wind-down plan, and cyber resilience framework; upon satisfactory review the RBNZ issues a no-objection letter and the operating authorization, following verification of the NZD 500,000 regulatory capital escrow held with a New Zealand registered bank.
required_dossiers: Authorized non-bank deposit taker / stored value facility application
Detailed business model description and legal opinions from New Zealand counsel
Tripartite escrow agreement with registered bank certificate
Three-year financial projections and capital adequacy plan
Cyber security, business continuity and incident response plans
Ownership structure, fit-and-proper declarations, and source of funds evidence
AML/CFT programme and FSP registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RBNZ raises prudential concerns, the applicant must deliver a Remedial Action Plan within 30 working days; the RBNZ may impose conditions, restrictions, or decline; an appeal lies to the High Court of New Zealand under the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013; during the appeal or remediation period, the FSP registration and AML/CFT registration remain enforceable, and the escrow amount must be maintained intact.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) — Financial Service Providers Register (lead licensing authority); Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) — Prudential Supervision Department (stored value / electronic money authorization); Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) — AML/CFT Group (AML supervision); WorkSafe New Zealand (occupational safety and health regulation).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Service Provider (FSP) Registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; and RBNZ 'Authorized Electronic Money / Stored Value Facility (Digital Wallet) Operator' and 'Virtual IBAN Issuer' prudential authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, operating under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, in conjunction with the local territorial authority (Auckland Council or Wellington City Council).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 — Low-risk Registration-Only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is required. The activity is a digital IT-based financial service with no industrial fabrication, no wastewater discharge, no atmospheric emissions, and no hazardous waste generation. The data center / cloud hosting provider must however comply with the National Environmental Standard for Telecommunication Facilities (2008) and local district plan 'permitted activity' thresholds; a Form 9 environmental registration (or equivalent certificate of compliance) is filed with the territorial authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge is permitted from the physical premises; any condensate or stormwater from data hosting must comply with the permitted-activity water quality standards (turbidity < 15 NTU, pH 6.5–8.5, suspended solids < 30 mg/L); electronic waste (e-waste) must be disposed of through an accredited registered e-waste recycler under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; volatile organic compound (VOC) emission limits are not applicable to the fintech activity, but building ventilation systems must meet ASHRAE 62.1 indoor air quality criteria; refrigerants in cooling systems must have a Global Warming Potential (GWP) below 2,500 pursuant to the Ozone Layer Protection Regulations 1996 (Montreal Protocol); server room noise must not exceed 45 dB(A) at the site boundary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ): Fire Safety Certificate and evacuation scheme approval under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, together with annual fire drill records. Building Act 2004: Building Warrant of Fitness (Form 12A) and annual structural load inspections for commercial premises, including server rack floor-load certification. WorkSafe New Zealand: Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 compliance registration, workplace risk assessment, occupational first aid certificate, electrical safety certification under the Electrical Workers Act 2010, and ergonomic work-station clearance. Civil Defence: registration of the business continuity and emergency response plan with the local Civil Defence and Emergency Management (CDEM) Group, including an earthquake-prone building assessment where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Tāke), Wellington, New Zealand; self-service portal: myIR (myIR.ird.govt.nz); business registration gateway: Business.govt.nz / NZBN
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a New Zealand IRD number (8- or 9-digit tax file number) before commencing taxable activity. For income tax, non-resident companies apply using form IR596 (Non-resident company registration) or through the myIR portal under the 'Register for an IRD number' workflow; a New Zealand tax agent or registered address for service is required. For Goods and Services Tax (GST), the same foreign entity registers online via myIR or the offshore supplier registration module; the applicant must provide certified company incorporation documents, proof of foreign tax residence (e.g., certificate of residence), and the physical address of the NZ branch or agent. Inland Revenue assigns a single IRD number for all taxes; there is no separate VAT/GST identification number. Processing takes 5-10 business days for paper applications and is generally instantaneous via myIR when identity verification is completed electronically.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box election system. Available statutory elections relevant to a non-resident International Company include: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election for NZ-resident closely held companies, not available to non-resident international companies; (2) Qualifying Company (QC) election, grandfathered for entities that elected before 2011, no longer open; (3) GST grouping election under s55 Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for related entities to file consolidated GST returns; (4) voluntary GST registration election before exceeding the NZD 60,000 threshold; (5) GST annual balance-date adjustment election; (6) zero-rating election for land transactions; (7) hybrid mismatch limitation rules (Income Tax Act 2007 ss FH 1-FH 15) apply automatically to cross-border arrangements, with no elective opt-out; any mismatch-based financing structure executed by the International Company is subject to mandatory adjustment rather than elective treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (taxable turnover in any rolling 12-month period). For non-resident offshore suppliers of remote services (including digital wallet and electronic money services) supplied to NZ consumers, mandatory registration arises when supplies to NZ exceed NZD 60,000 per annum; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. A related-person aggregation rule applies to determine the NZD 60,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol BIS 3.0 standard via accredited Access Points; Inland Revenue does not operate an API-based tax clearance gateway for invoice issuance. Tax invoices may be issued on paper, by PDF, or through Peppol. E-invoicing adoption is promoted by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, but there is no statutory obligation to obtain Inland Revenue pre-approval, fiscal stamp, or sequential pre-registered invoice numbering before issuing a tax invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exports is governed by section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Eligibility to apply 0% GST requires: (a) for goods, the goods are exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply and the supplier retains evidence of physical export; (b) for services supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, the services must be performed outside New Zealand or, for remote/digital services, supplied for consumption outside New Zealand (B2B supplies to non-resident recipients outside NZ qualify for zero-rating even if the service is received remotely); (c) the supply is directly in connection with goods exported from New Zealand; or (d) the supply is a taxable supply to a non-resident that would otherwise be exempt financial services, in which case the 'offshore services' rule zero-rates the fee if the non-resident recipient is outside New Zealand at the time of supply. Electronic money issuance, Virtual IBAN setup fees, and wallet reserve management fees supplied to non-resident corporate clients are zero-rated under the offshore services provisions, provided the non-resident recipient is outside New Zealand and the services are not supplied to an NZ consumer. Standard 15% GST applies to supplies of remote services to New Zealand resident consumers, including platform users in NZ.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (TID / EMSAC declaration filed electronically with New Zealand Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Airway Bill (air) evidencing physical departure of goods from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign-exchange receipt evidencing payment received from the overseas buyer
Proof of export (port/airport examination or customs clearance records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue actively audits zero-rated export supplies, remote services, and GST refund claims. Where zero-rating is claimed without substantiating documentation or where an exporter fails to export goods within 28 days, the supply is subject to 15% GST retrospectively, and any input credits previously claimed are clawed back with use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Civil shortfall penalties apply: 20% for lack of reasonable care; 40% for gross carelessness; 100% for knowingly taking an unacceptable tax position; 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution for GST evasion under s143A TAA can result in imprisonment and fines up to NZD 50,000. Under s36A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, directors and senior officers may be personally liable for GST debts incurred during their tenure if the company fails to pay. For an International Company, mischaracterisation of financial services as zero-rated offshore services triggers full recovery of GST output tax on all historical supplies plus penalties, and may invalidate the entity's tax-exempt classification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the apex central bank supervising the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), the high-value clearing system, and the regulatory framework for banks and non-bank deposit takers. Foreign exchange policy is administered through the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021, while AML/CFT supervision is shared with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has full current and capital account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange control laws, no prior approval requirements for cross-border capital movements, and no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or liquidation proceeds. Foreign investors may repatriate capital and earnings freely through licensed banks. The only practical remittance hurdles are of a tax nature: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on interest, dividends, and royalties; approved issuer levy (AIL) options; and thin capitalization rules for foreign-owned entities. No central bank consent or foreign exchange allocation permit is required to convert NZD into any foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand has no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no compulsory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters freely retain proceeds in offshore accounts or in New Zealand bank accounts in supported foreign currencies. The only ongoing obligations relate to AML/CFT record-keeping on the origin and destination of funds and Inland Revenue attribution rules for controlled foreign company income where relevant. No percentage of export proceeds must be converted to NZD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational NZD Account with multi-currency sweep
Operational Transaction Account with Foreign Currency Pack
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Finance (Commercial LC) Account
Operational Account with Offshore-Capable Global Trade and FX Solutions
Operational Account only, aligned to locally-domiciled activity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — restricted but achievable through a licensed bank partnership model. No direct pass-porting regime exists for EU/UK/offshore digital EMI licences into New Zealand; an foreign EMI cannot become a direct participant in the New Zealand retail payment system (Automated Payment Service) or the high-value ESAS clearing system. The commercially viable route is to contract with one or more Tier 1 New Zealand registered banks to act as settlement sponsor and underlying account provider, while the EMI issues virtual IBANs and digital wallets as a registered financial service provider under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008. The entity must also comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and register with the FMA and DIA as a reporting entity. The issuance of stored-value facilities and e-money itself is not a prohibited activity in New Zealand but requires full AML/CFT compliance and transparency on reserve safeguarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand does not impose an absolute statutory obligation for physical in-branch attendance. Tier 1 banks generally accept a high-definition live video interview for corporate onboarding where overseas directors present certified passport copies, a certified power of attorney, a New Zealand-registered local agent, and a physical registered office address in New Zealand. However, for a non-resident-owned entity classified as an International Company operating under a special EMI license, most major banks will mandate a physical or notarized appearance before a New Zealand legal counsel or an authorized bank representative in the jurisdiction of the director's residence. A remote onboarding outcome is achievable only when a reputable New Zealand law firm independently verifies identity and holds original documents. Directorship and beneficial ownership attestations via secure video are increasingly accepted, but full physical appearance remains the safest route for expedited account approval and clearing system membership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity nomenclature and structuring resembling a classic offshore International Company with corporate secrecy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation or registration, current constitution, registered office certificate, consolidated register of members, beneficial ownership declaration, board resolution appointing signatories, statutory declaration of economic substance for EMI licensing, New Zealand tax resident status confirmation, and CRS/FATCA self-certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management flagged as high-risk payment intermediary activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved AML/CFT compliance program, independent audit report by an FMA-recognized AML compliance officer, transaction monitoring system certification, transaction screening rules, segregation of client reserve funds evidence, regulatory license or in-principle approval for the special EMI license, and external verifiable proof of robust operational resilience.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt zone classification raising presumptions of tax evasion or round-tripping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: New Zealand Inland Revenue confirmation that the entity is not exploiting an artificial arrangement; documented economic substance with local employees or licensed agent presence; full CRS and FATCA declarations; financial statements prepared under NZ IFRS; board minutes evidencing commercial substance; and zero adverse tax rulings or penalties history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners residing in or connected to sanctioned or higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified source of wealth report, certified source of funds report, professional legal and accounting references, sanctions and adverse-media screening results from an independent provider, enhanced due diligence questionnaires, sworn declarations of legal origin of funds, and a guarantee letter from the sponsor relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows touching cryptocurrency exchanges or unregulated digital assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction flow heat-mapping or documented purpose codes for all digital asset interactions, whitelist of approved exchange counterparties, evidence of AML/CFT strength of counterparty exchanges, reserve custody audit certificates, and a legal opinion confirming that digital wallet operations remain within the permissible scope of the special license.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 credits to the entity's NZD operational or escrow account at a Tier 1 New Zealand bank, citing an appropriate purpose code such as 'EQUI' for equity capital formation or 'INTC' for intercompany loan funding. The remitter should include the entity's NZ Business Number (NZBN), IRD number, the share subscription agreement, board resolution, and a certificate of inward payment issued by the receiving bank where the commercial bank requires it. All funds must emanate from a banking account held in the name of the beneficial investor or declared financing party; the purpose of payment field must state 'Capital Contribution under Share Subscription' or 'Shareholder Loan under International Company Constitution', never generic terms. There are no exchange surrender obligations and no New Zealand Reserve Bank approvals; verification of source of funds is the bank's principal gatekeeper.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements from New Zealand are executed via SWIFT MT103 for open account trade settlements, ISO 20022 pacs.008 for low-value GBP and EUR corridors, SWIFT MT700/MT707 for documentary letters of credit issuance and amendments, and SWIFT MT760 for standby letters of credit guarantees. NZD-denominated interbank payments clear through the Reserve Bank's ESAS high-value settlement system; USD clearings route over CHIPS or Fedwire; EUR clearings settle via TARGET2/SEPA Credit Transfer; GBP clearings settle via CHAPS. Commercial banks in the Tier 1 group provide trade finance desks to support import/export transactions with cargo documentation review, discrepancy handling, and purchase-order financing, all subject to standard AML/CFT referral for underlying invoices and customs declarations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright and tom-next FX forward contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/CNH) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with New Zealand Law Schedule or the New Zealand Financial Markets Association AMF Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or managed currencies such as CNY (via CNH reference rate), IDR, PHP, VND, and KRW where a Tier 1 New Zealand bank maintains an approved NDF desk and obtains internal market-risk approval
Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNH) utilised to hedge long-dated EMI reserve assets or to align funding and settlement currencies
FX swaps (swap/roll) for short-term liquidity conversion between NZD and foreign currency nostro balances
Vanilla call and put FX options for asymmetric hedging of reserve float exposure against adverse rate movements
Currency interest-rate basis swaps combining interest-rate and foreign-exchange risk hedges for multi-currency wallet float portfolios

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty applies after the due date; if the company remains non-compliant, the Registrar issues a 20 working-day notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand register under section 318 Companies Act 1993, after which the company is struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (for large or non-exempt companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders as at the balance date; filed with Companies Office if the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the company's balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors commit an offence for failure to prepare and present financial statements; individual directors are liable to fines up to NZD 10,000 and the company up to NZD 50,000; continued failure is reported to the Registrar and may trigger deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and accompanying statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, filed by 7 July of the same year; for an early balance date, within 4 months after balance date; further extension to 31 March of the following year if a tax agent is engaged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 plus interest; late payment penalty of 1% per month on unpaid tax; persistent non-filing may prompt IRD prosecution and enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Financial Service Providers, Companies Office, MBIE, New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of FSP registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation causes the registration to lapse; the entity is derecognised from FSPR, loses its statutory licence to provide financial services, and continued unregistered trading may incur civil penalties and FMA prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT programme independent review and annual compliance confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (AML/CFT supervisor for financial service providers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Independent review at least once every two years under section 58 AML/CFT Act 2009; annual internal compliance confirmation completed before the company's financial year-end review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance under the AML/CFT Act 2009 is subject to civil pecuniary penalties up to NZD 2 million for a body corporate and NZD 200,000 for an individual, plus daily penalties; FMA may suspend or revoke the financial service provider registration and take enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required if the company is not exempt under section 211 Companies Act 1993 and is classified as 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, i.e., total assets exceed NZD 60 million, total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million, or the company is an FMC reporting entity or licensed financial institution; a licensed electronic-money institution will ordinarily be a regulated entity and must be audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must comply with New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP); for-profit entities report under NZ IFRS (Tier 1) or the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return filed with the Companies Office must set out the current registered shareholders and directors. Register of Members entries must reflect any share transfers completed within the year. As a licensed financial institution, the entity must maintain up-to-date beneficial ownership files for every customer and counterparty under the AML/CFT Act 2009; any shareholder holding 25% or more or with control over the company is re-verified and confirmed annually on the internal UBO register, and the next annual return must be updated within 10 working days of any material change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (New Zealand corporate income tax rate under Schedule 1, Part A, clause 2, Income Tax Act 2007)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No territorial tax-exempt zone exists under New Zealand law; an entity described as an 'International Company' is taxable at 28% on worldwide income if resident. Refundable R&D tax credit of 15% on eligible expenditure (Income Tax Act 2007, subparts LY-LZ) is available. Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, not for 5 years, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test or the business continuity test.
